beliefs.practice: Read the cluster connection string from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) and never commit live credentials; use a placeholder .env.example in repo instead.
Create a single MongoClient (pymongo.MongoClient) at application startup and reuse it for all requests; close it on shutdown (do not create a new client per request).

Pack float32 embedding vectors into BSON Binary using pymongo.binary.Binary with the designated subtype (use the vector-subtype your server expects — e.g., 0x09 in this sample) rather than storing arrays of 512 floats, and unpack with numpy.frombuffer(dtype=np.float32).

Always normalize embeddings (L2 normalize to unit length) before storing and before querying if you want cosine similarity to be equivalent to inner product on the server index; document the normalization in each stored document (e.g., store a 'normed': true flag or store raw + normalized).

Store vector dimensionality and dtype as explicit metadata fields (e.g., embedding_dim=512, embedding_dtype='float32') on each document or in a collection-level schema document and validate on insert to prevent mismatched vector lengths.

Prefer server-side vector indexes/search when the cluster supports them; detect capability at startup (listIndexes/listCommands or try a dry-run) and fall back to client-side approximate search only when server-side vector queries/indexes are unavailable.

When creating a vector index do it idempotently: check existing indexes with list_indexes/listIndexes and only call create_index/createIndexes if the desired index is absent; catch and handle server rejections (bad option names) instead of failing startup.
Do not log the DOCUMENTDB_URI or any credentials; redact connection strings and error messages that may contain secrets in application logs.

Use Binary subtype support from the driver (pymongo.binary.Binary) and verify the cluster accepts that subtype for vector fields; when unsure, probe by inserting a small test document and/or consult the server's docs for the exact subtype expected by its vector index implementation.
Use dtype float32 for embeddings and avoid BSON arrays of float64 (the Mongo default) to reduce storage and bandwidth; pack/unpack consistently and test roundtrip equality in unit tests.

Implement exponential-backoff retries with jitter for transient network errors and server-selected timeouts; enable driver-level retryReads/retryWrites when supported by the server and safe for your operations, and make retry behavior configurable.
Limit the fields returned by visual-search queries (projection) to only what the client needs (e.g., product_id, image_url, score) to reduce network transfer and latency.

When seeding demo or sample data, use upsert operations and a known, dedicated database (sample_retail_11) and collection name (products); avoid touching other databases or collections on the live cluster.

Detect and respect the server's supported wire protocol/features (MongoDB version, vector index types such as IVF/HNSW/DiskANN) at runtime—query server buildInfo or isMaster/hello—and adapt index creation parameters to that server's accepted syntax rather than assuming a single API format.

Protect the /visual-search upload endpoint: validate content-type, limit upload size, enforce timeouts, and reject non-image files to avoid DoS and avoid decoding extremely large images in-memory; return clear 4xx errors for invalid input.

Keep embedding encoding deterministic for reproducibility in tests (pin model version or use a deterministic fallback encoder in CI) and include unit tests to verify pack/unpack identity and deterministic outputs for fixed inputs.

Use server-side index build settings that minimize disruption: create indexes during maintenance windows, use the server's recommended background/online options, and monitor CPU/disk usage when building large vector indexes (createIndexes can be expensive).

Instrument and monitor vector-search-specific metrics (index size, index build time, query latency, RAM/IO used by ANN algorithms) and integrate with Azure Monitor/metrics when running on DocumentDB so you can detect index regressions and high-cost queries.

Use listIndexes/listIndexes on the collection to verify that the vector-ivf (or chosen algorithm) index actually exists and has the expected parameters after creation; if createIndex fails, capture the error and fall back or surface a clear admin message.

Avoid transferring all embeddings to the client for search in production; if the server lacks vector search, provision a small dedicated ANN service (FAISS/Annoy/HNSWlib) or do batched approximate operations rather than naive full-table brute-force queries.
